questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country and some international recognition towards the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It could’ve been easier, but I got a lot of information from the University of Melbourne helping quite a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction day at campus and an intro week, which felt quite redundant, but you had the opportunity to sign up for some social and athletic clubs

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is in a housing crisis, which means that many people both scam and take advantage of students including university. A standard small dormitory room with just a bed and a desk would easily be priced at more than 7000 DKK/month. It would recommend doing an Airbnb or hostel the first two weeks and then go hunting, once you get there. It pays off a lot in the long run.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Go for Fitzroy, Carlton, Parkville or any neighbor suburb.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only a slightly outdated it system caused a bit of frustration and the schedule could easily be overbooked if you didn’t go for subjects with flexibility in their planning. They do however record everything (at the science and medicine faculties at least), which makes everything a lot easier regarding catching up.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a login to their web page, where you follow the instructions. Beforehand, you can look everything up in their handbook, which describes every subject, course etc. with prerequisites, learning outcomes and everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guide, it’s quite simple, but can take some time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was similar to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They have a lot less of independency, which annoyed me a lot, as I was forced to follow a tutor, while in lab. It just sent redundant and stupid. This is a general thing, where they differ a bit in mentality from DK. Besides that, it was similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration, Australia in the Wine World, Microbes, Infections and Responses, and Foundations of Computing.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Australia in the Wine World is a nice and easy way to get into some Aussie culture and jargon, and also have some wonderful wine. The Stem Cell subject offers a lot more flexibility and independency compared to the other subjects. Computing is done in Pyhton and works quite well with the help of a program called Grok, but it’s only if you haven’t done coding before.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing major, if you’ve done your homework.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and electronics. Alcohol is more expensive tho.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Do the surf club, but make sure to follow them on IG, as you have to run to a secret place they announce there in order to go on camps. It’s stressful, but the camps are worth it. The later ones are generally easier to get in on. The mountaineering club is also recommendable.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. Follow UMSU and Unimelb Sport and go to intro week to see it all.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf club and mountaineering club activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wilsons Prom (you can go on very long, isolated, and beautiful hikes there for multiple days), Philips Island (to see wildlife), Great Ocean Road (surf here e.g. in Torquay or Lorne), The Grampians, Ballarat, Yarra Valley, Mornington Peninsula, Dandenong.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, but they can be difficult to understand at times.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendly mentality and laid back style of life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don’t be too academic (choose easier subjects), go on as many trips as possible, meet some locals either via shared housing or social clubs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find a place to live close to campus and life. I recommend Carlton, Fitzroy or Brunswick.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of tests and quizzes that contribute to your final grade. That’s annoying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
